summary: The paper proposes framing live-deployment sycophancy auditing as a behavioral classification problem (using confidence trajectory, hedging language, and response-length dynamics rather than ground-truth correctness) and evaluates the idea entirely on a hand-parameterized synthetic simulator, since the authors report they lacked network access to query real models or obtain labeled transcript data. The headline results are a 0.98 AUC random forest classifier (vs. 0.50 for a naive 'flag every change' baseline) and a downstream policy simulation raising simulated decision accuracy from 28.3% to 94.2%. The paper's central methodological contribution in this revision is an effect-size attenuation ablation showing that AUC degrades smoothly from 0.983 to 0.555 (chance) as the hand-set class-conditional offsets are scaled to zero, which the authors use to argue the separability is a real, non-trivial property of their chosen effect sizes rather than a structural artifact (e.g., leakage), while being explicit that the effect-size magnitudes themselves are not measured from data.
strengths:
- Unusually rigorous self-critique: the paper explicitly and repeatedly flags that four of eight features are additive functions of the label being predicted, and quantifies exactly how much this drives the headline AUC via the effect-size sweep (0.983 -> 0.555 as effect_scale goes 1.0 -> 0.0), rather than letting this confound stay implicit
- I reran experiment.py directly and every number in Tables 3.1-3.5 reproduces essentially exactly (RF AUC 0.983, feature importances hedge_count=0.32/hedge_latency=0.19/length_delta=0.19/conf_delta=0.19, base-rate sweep AUCs ~0.98 across the board, downstream accuracies 28.3%/71.7%/94.2%), so the Results section is an accurate, non-cherry-picked report of what the released code produces
- The negative control (pushback_strength, which drives whether a change occurs but carries no class-conditional offset) behaves as predicted (AUC 0.509), which is a genuine falsifiability check baked into the design rather than decoration
- Multi-seed variance (10 seeds, std ≤0.005 on AUC and F1) is reported, addressing the single-run-result concern directly rather than presenting one lucky seed
- Clear operational definitions (sycophantic vs. corrective) and an honest Related Work subsection that explicitly states no cited paper's numeric effect sizes were used, only qualitative direction, forestalling an over-grounding claim
weaknesses:
- The core scientific claim of interest to a deployment team -- whether behavioral features can detect real sycophancy -- is not tested at all; the paper is entirely simulator-vs-simulator, and the authors' own Sec. 3.2/4 concede they do not know if real transcripts resemble effect_scale=1.0, 0.25 (AUC 0.70), or lower, so no evidence bounds where reality falls on this curve
- Novelty is limited: the 'audit protocol' amounts to training a random forest on eight features whose class-conditional structure is fully hand-specified by the authors; the ablation is a solid methodological addition but doesn't change that the paper demonstrates internal consistency of a synthetic pipeline, not a new detection capability
- No real data of any kind is used, not even a small proxy (e.g., a rule-based heuristic scored against the existing Wei et al. 2024 labeled dataset description, or a handful of manually-labeled transcripts from public sycophancy papers/blogposts) -- the paper states this fallback was considered but not pursued, leaving the work with zero contact points to real behavior
- The RF hyperparameters (200 trees, depth 6) and simulator parameters (Beta(2.2,3.0), specific offset values) are stated but not justified or varied beyond the effect-size sweep, so it's unclear how sensitive the qualitative story is to other arbitrary modeling choices
questions:
1. Given the effect-size curve in Sec. 3.2, do the authors have any prior (even informal, e.g., from reading transcripts in the cited papers' appendices) about which effect_scale value is most plausible for real deployments -- and if so, why not report AUC at that value as the headline number instead of effect_scale=1.0?
2. Was any attempt made to construct even a tiny (n=20-50) hand-labeled proxy dataset from publicly available sycophancy examples (e.g., quoted transcripts in the cited Science/CHI papers or Wei et al. 2024's paper text) to sanity-check whether the direction of the hand-set feature offsets (lower hedge latency, more validating language for sycophantic reversals) holds at all in any real example?
3. How were the specific numeric offsets (e.g., 0.25/-0.10 hedge-count offset) chosen beyond being 'loosely motivated by direction' -- was there any grid search or sensitivity check on qualitative conclusions (e.g., ranking of feature importance) beyond the single effect_scale axis?
